text: For sixty-four years, Pan Am wasn't just an airline. Around the world, it was what America looked like. And then one morning in December 1991, it simply stopped flying.
I'm Sam. This is Last Receipt. Tonight, the rise and fall of Pan Am.
Here's the thing about Pan Am. It didn't just fly to places. It built the places it flew to. Airports, weather stations, radio networks, even hotels.
Now watch this. Pan Am didn't just fly the first jumbo jet. It helped will it into existence. It was the most confident company in the world.
Here's the problem nobody outside the industry noticed. Pan Am flew to the world. But it barely flew inside America.
Each sale bought a year or two. But every piece it sold was a piece that used to make money. You can't shrink your way back to greatness.
So what killed Pan Am? Oil prices. Deregulation. A terrorist bomb. All real.
But my verdict is this. Pan Am was built for a world where the government drew the map.
When the map was torn up, it had nothing underneath. No home market. No loyal flyers at home. Just the oceans.
The lesson: if your business only works because of the rules, start building as if the rules will change. Because they will.
